newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia iron ore exports to rise - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia iron ore exports to rise - ABARE.

text.p: Australian iron ore exports are forecast to increase in 1996/97 to June 30 to address higher demand from integrated steel makers in China, Japan and Europe, the government's key commodity forecaster said on Tuesday.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its December quarter Commodities publication that Australian iron ore exports would rise 9.8 million tonnes to around 136 million tonnes in 1996/97.
The latest forecast is slightly above the increase of 7.0 million tonnes to 133.5 million tonnes predicted in the September quarter report.

ABARE said stocks would be used to supply much of the increase in shipments with production expected to rise 3.3 million tonnes to 151 million tonnes. "A significant proportion of the increase in demand (from China, Japan and Europe) will be met by increased exports from Australia and Brazil," ABARE said.

"The value of Australian iron ore exports is forecast to rise by A$259 million to A$3.1 billion in 1996/97, with increased volumes and prices offsetting the effects of an assumed further appreciation of the Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar," it said. The forecast for value of exports is in line with ABARE's September quarter prediction.
